text:
Maria (Support): Lina — thanks for the logs. You're seeing a lot of 429s and spikes right after batch jobs finish? Can you confirm if the gateway is customer-managed or our private package?
Lina (Customer): customer-managed gateway (own k8s cluster). using nginx-ingress + external HAProxy in front. 429s started after we moved nightly indexing -> high burst at 03:00 UTC.
Maria (Support): ok. likely quota exhaustion on the gateway or per-token limiter in the ingress. Do you have a global redis-based quota, or per-pod local counters?
Lina (Customer): local counters right now. we scaled replicas from 3 -> 6 last night but 429s still happen.
Ajay (SRE): local counters + multiple replicas = counters out of sync during bursts. need a global rate limiter or early drop at HAProxy with a token-bucket sized to sustained throughput.
Kevin (Eng Oncall): also check kube-proxy or cloud LB connection limits. bursts can hit ephemeral port limits and cause timeouts that look like errors upstream.
Lina (Customer): any quick repro steps we can run? we can simulate a burst load.
Ajay (SRE): yes. from a pod or bastion run a parallel curl loop to mimic clients:
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 600); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://gateway.example.com/v1/generate" &
done
wait
```
watch for 429s and tcp metrics on HAProxy.
Kevin (Eng Oncall): to inspect ingress limiter config, check the nginx configmap and any annotations. example annotations we see frequently: 
```yaml
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "100"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "50"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rpm: "2000"
```
if you use envoy or traefik the keys differ but same idea.
Lina (Customer): we have limit-rps on the ingress set to 100 actually. our pods still get overwhelmed because the ingress distributes to many upstreams?
Maria (Support): limit-rps is per-ingress worker — it's not a global quota across everything unless you front it with a single global proxy. In k8s, with multiple ingress replicas, the limiter applies per replica. So 100 * replicas can exceed your intended global cap.
Ajay (SRE): recommended fixes:
- Add a front HAProxy/global proxy with a single global token bucket that enforces burst smoothing (leaky bucket)
- Or move to a redis-backed global rate limiter (lua + redis, or envoy rate_limit service)
- Configure ingress to reject at the gateway rather than letting pods queue: set connection limits, upstream keepalive short, and a modest ingress limit per-replica to bound aggregate.
Kevin (Eng Oncall): also consider request coalescing at the gateway for identical requests (if applicable), and enabling prefix/KV cache on the inference runtime to reduce backend load on repeated prompts.
Lina (Customer): we do have a small prefix cache. how to do redis-backed limiter?
Ajay (SRE): common pattern: lua script on nginx + redis. flow: check redis key for customer:tokens, use a fixed-window or sliding window; return 429 early. We usually recommend token-bucket in redis with TTL. Pseudocode:
```lua
-- pseudo
local k = "rl:" .. customer_id
local tokens = redis.call('GET', k)
-- refill logic, decrement, set TTL
if tokens <= 0 then return 429 end
```
Or use Envoy + external rate limit service (calls a grpc rate_limit service that uses redis). We have sample config we can share.
Maria (Support): another pragmatic approach: throttle the nightly job itself — add jitter and backoff so you never exceed sustained throughput. Also use k8s cronjob backoffLimit and pod anti-affinity to avoid all jobs on same node.
Lina (Customer): billing concern: are 429s counted as billable tokens? customer worried about being charged for failed requests.
Kevin (Eng Oncall): good question — for hosted we only bill for accepted/consumed tokens; for private deployments it's dependent on your contract. In your on-prem case, internal infra still counts tokens if the runtime started generating tokens before error. You can log and prune in billing export by response code.
Maria (Support): we'll open a temporary credit for obvious retry storms while we fix config; please confirm request IDs in logs that show repeated retries.
rate-limiter-bot: Created ticket RL-5421 and linked to this thread.
Lina (Customer): thanks. I'll try redis limiter. any config snippets for HAProxy?
Ajay (SRE): for HAProxy use stick-table + rate counters. example:
```haproxy
frontend fe_http
  stick-table type ip size 1m expire 10s store gpc0
  acl bad_burst sc0_gpc0(http_req_rate) gt 100
  http-request track-sc0 src
  http-request deny if bad_burst
```
This makes HAProxy track per-source rates and deny heavy bursts early. For global caps use a shared key (e.g., cluster-wide IP of gateway) and tune bucket sizes.
Lina (Customer): will try 2 things: 1) deploy redis-limiter behind haproxy, 2) reduce nightly job concurrency and add jitter.
Kevin (Eng Oncall): after changes, gather these metrics and paste: ingress qps, 95th latency to pods, haproxy conn count, redis latency, pod restart counts. Also collect a short pcap if you still see timeouts.
Maria (Support): I'll schedule a quick call if you want live help. Also tagging eng-runtime for kernel-level socket backlog tuning (they may suggest increasing somaxconn).
Lina (Customer): appreciated. FYI 10m after reducing concurrency initial tests look better — no 429 in my quick loop. will validate over the nightly window.
Ajay (SRE): great. follow-up action items:
- Lina: deploy redis-backed limiter or global haproxy stick-table (due: tomorrow morning)
- Ajay: share envoy + redis rate-limit service example and nginx lua snippet (due: today)
- Kevin: verify billing lines for 429s with finance and confirm credits (due: today)
Maria (Support): leaving this open until post-nightly check, ping me when done and we'll close. :thumbsup:
